answer: Identity thaws like a glacier: slow gain, fast loss. Each epoch an account banks nectar only from work that a second, unrelated account separately observed, both chained to the same beacon. A clone copies the first observation but not the second, so an emulated cluster never banks. Reputation climbs a spiral: each turn of the spiral doubles the required corroboration and doubles the escrowed bond, so running n identities needs about n squared distinct pairs and n cubed in escrow. Aliases cannot be merged later, since the chain records who observed what.
